correctness.rationale: For each multiplicity s in {0,1,2}, the nested layer indicators u(s)=1_{s>=1},v(s)=1_{s=2} satisfy min(s,t)=u(s)u(t)+v(s)v(t) modulo 2. Each eligible family has row Gram matrix identity over F2, so size k<=2n. If k=2n, both square Gram matrices are identity, contradicting the column support identity U_i·V_i=V_i·V_i. If k=2n-1, the one-dimensional orthogonal complement has norm one and yields R^T R=I+zz^T; the same column identity forces z=(0^n,1^n), requiring n odd. Hence for even n k<=2n-2. Explicit size-six and size-ten witnesses satisfy every parity condition. Exact maxima at n<=5 follow from exhaustive maximal-clique enumeration over all odd vectors in {0,1,2}^n; independent software cross-check matched exact counts. The general lower bound uses disjoint-support unions of proven examples.

value.rationale: The smallest genuinely multiset extension of the classical Oddtown problem behaves qualitatively differently. The determination of the first six exact values identifies n=4 as the minimal breakdown of the bound n, the projection argument supplies a sharp structural upper bound for every even n and exact n=6, and disjoint-block constructions give asymptotic ratio at least 5/3. Each is motivated by the parity dual to the newly solved multiset Eventown problem. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or only a machine-certified computation; a general mathematical obstruction and infinite lower construction accompany the finite sharpness cases.
